Anthracnose.quote: Irregular brown spots develop in a random pattern on stems and pods.
Infected leaves may develop brown veins and curl up.

Bacterial_Blight.quote: Angular lesions, which begin as small yellow to brown spots on the leaves.

Bacterial_Pustule.quote: A pustule may form in the center of some lesions, usually on the lower leaf surface.

Bean_Pod_Mottle_Virus.quote: Foliar symptoms caused by Bean pod mottle virus (BPMV) include distorted and wrinkled leaves that have a mottled color pattern.
Infection by BPMV decreases pod formation, reduces seed size, weight and number, and may cause seed mottling.

Brown_Spot.quote: Infected young plants have purple lesions on the unifoliate leaves. Lesions on later leaves are small, irregularly shaped, dark brown, and are found on both leaf surfaces.

Brown_Stem_Rot.quote: internal browning of vascular tissue and pith is evident, especially at nodes and in the lower stem
chlorosis and necrosis between leaf veins, followed by leaf curling and leaf death

Cercospora.quote: Foliar symptoms usually are seen at the beginning of seed set and occur in the uppermost canopy on leaves exposed to the sun.
Seeds infected with this pathogen can be symptomless or have pink to purple spots extending from the hilum.

Charcoal_Rot.quote: The fungus produces numerous tiny, black fungal structures called microsclerotia that are scattered throughout the pith and on the surface of taproots and lower stems.

Diaporthe.quote: black, raised specks that appear in linear rows on mature soybean stems
black structures may also cover pods, but they may not follow the linear pattern seen on stems
cracked, shriveled seed with white chalk-colored mold on the seed surface

Downy_Mildew.quote: Lesions occur on upper leaf surfaces as irregularly shaped, pale green to light yellow spots that enlarge into pale to bright yellow spots.
Downy mildew-infected pods show no external symptoms, but the inside of the pod and seed may be covered with a dried, whitish fungal mass that appears crusty and contains spores.
Infected seed can be smaller, appear dull white and have cracks in the seed coat.

Frogeye_Leaf_Spot.quote: Frogeye leaf spot initially appears on upper leaf surfaces as small, dark, water-soaked spots (lesions).
Pod lesions appear oblong and resemble foliar symptoms.
The fungus that causes frogeye leaf spot may infect seeds, which results in light purple to gray discoloration, but infected seed also may not show any symptoms.

Fusarium_Disease.quote: Root rot appears as reddish-brown to dark brown discolored roots and poor nodulation.
Infected plants have brown vascular tissue in the roots and stems and show wilting of the stem tips.
Foliar symptoms of Fusarium wilt include scorching of the upper leaves, while middle and lower canopy leaves can turn chlorotic and later wither and drop from the plant.

Green_Stem.quote: Stems of plants remain green after the pods and seeds have ripened and are brown and ready for harvest.

Herbicide_Injury.quote: Dicamba often causes leaf cupping (Figure 6), but veins at the tips of the leaves may be parallel and stretched (Figure 7).
Severe injury from a misapplication of high rates of any HG 4 product causes epinasty or twisting of the stems within a few days of application, at lower doses epinasty may be absent.

Iron_Deficiency_Chlorosis.quote: Symptoms appear on newly formed leaves, often starting with the first trifoliate leaves, because iron (Fe) is not mobile within the plant.

Phyllosticta_Leaf_Spot.quote: Lesions most often occur on leaves and are circular, oval, and irregular or V-shaped.

Phytophthora.quote: The most characteristic symptom of Phytophthora root and stem rot is a dark brown lesion on the lower stem that extends up from the taproot of the plant.
The lesion often reaches as high as several nodes and will girdle soybean stems, restricting flow of nutrients and water, and stunting or killing the plant.

Potassium_Deficiency.quote: Potassium (K) deficiency symptoms appear as a yellowing of the leaves that begins at the tip and extends along edges or margins and continues toward the base as severity increases.

Powdery_Mildew.quote: The most common and characteristic sign of powdery mildew is white, powdery fungal growth that can cover all aboveground plant parts, particularly the upper leaf surface.

Rhizoctonia.quote: Infected seedlings have reddish-brown lesions on the hypocotyls at the soil line. These lesions are sunken and remain firm and dry.
Reddish-brown lesions form on infected petioles, stems, pods and petiole scars.
First leaf symptoms appear as water-soaked, grayish green lesions that turn tan to brown at maturity.

Rust.quote: Lesions start to form on lower leaf surfaces as small, gray spots that change to tan or reddish-brown.

Soybean_Cyst_Nematode.quote: Noticeable symptoms of SCN include stunting, slow or no canopy closure, and chlorotic foliage.
During the cropping season, SCN is relatively easy to detect without magnification as small, white or yellow, lemon-shaped females (immature cysts) on the root surface.

Soybean_Mosaic_Virus.quote: Foliar symptoms caused by Soybean mosaic virus (SMV) include distorted and wrinkled leaves that have a mottled color pattern.
The major concern with soybean mosaic is reduced seed quality due to mottled seeds.

Soybean_Vein_Necrosis_Virus.quote: Symptoms caused by Soybean vein necrosis virus (SVNV) often begin as yellowing near leaf veins that develops into reddish-brown lesions, causing death of leaf tissue.

Tobacco_Streak_Virus.quote: Symptoms of Tobacco streak virus (TSV) include bud blight, shepherd's crooking, stunting, wilting, delayed maturity, bud and leaf proliferation, reduced pod number, and discolored, distorted, and dead leaves.
TSV infection can cause discoloration and dead streaks at nodes, dark spots on pods, and delayed seed development.

White_Mold.quote: Initial symptoms generally develop from R3 to R6 as gray to white lesions at the nodes, and lesions rapidly progress above and below the nodes, sometimes girdling the stem.
Initial foliar symptoms include leaf tissues between major veins turning a gray-green cast; eventually leaves die and turn completely brown while remaining attached to the stem.
